newsitem.title: CANADA: Campbell moves ahead on Panama gold play.
newsitem.headline: Campbell moves ahead on Panama gold play.

text.p: Campbell Resources Inc said on Monday that it had completed a positive feasibility study on the Cerro Quema gold project in Panama.

The board of directors had given approval to go ahead with the next stage of the development which will include engineering and construction, at a cost of US$1.4 million, the company said in a statement.
A final mine plan has been submitted to Panamanian authorities and permits are expected by January 1997 at which time final approval of the project is expected, Campbell said.
Production should start by the first quarter of 1998.
The feasibility study recommends a low cost, open pit, heap leach gold mine with production of 50,000 ounces of gold per year over a six-year mine life.
Capital costs are estimated at US$32.8 million and will be paid for by the company's internal funds, Campbell said.
Cash costs will be about US$180 an ounce. The project will bring Campbell's total gold production to more than 170,000 ounces a year by 1998, the company said.
